html:
SMTO-FIL-0018 — SMTO couldn't find that file or folder

GUID: 7a813a8e-d503-47a8-8df7-4253a1cc3b50
Slug: file-not-found
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • A file, folder, drive or network location SMTO needed isn't there on the selected computer. It may have been moved, renamed or deleted, or SMTO is looking on the wrong computer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check which Gateway is selected for your message, and make sure it is the computer that actually has the file. The same location can exist on one computer and be missing on another.
  2. On that computer, check that the file and the folders above it exist with exactly those names. If it moved, tell SMTO its new full location. SMTO needs the current name and place; a renamed folder anywhere along the way causes this error.
  3. If the file is on a USB drive or network share, reconnect it. A disconnected drive looks to SMTO like a missing file.
  4. Ask SMTO to look in the folder again before it repeats the step. A fresh look gives SMTO the current names instead of ones it remembered.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the file or folder and the step completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to recreate the file from memory if the original may have only moved; you could end up with two different versions.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation found a required path, drive or network location absent: the OS returned ENOENT or a Windows not-found code, write mode replace/append targeted a missing file, a patch target's parent directory is missing, or a transfer source does not exist.

What this means

  • The OS reported a missing path/drive/network location, or update/patch/transfer preconditions require an existing item or parent that is absent. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The OS reported a missing path/drive/network location, or update/patch/transfer preconditions require an existing item or parent that is absent.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact Gateway, operand and required parent; a normal stat exists:false result is distinct from this failure.

How to fix it

  • Check path_context/resolved_path and the selected Gateway node in the receipt, then list the parent directory on that Gateway. Correct the path or Gateway selection, mount the missing drive or share, or use write mode create with create_parents when creating the item is intended (gateway_core/file_common.error_kind, file_mutate.write, file_patch.patch, transfer.TransferProvider._open).
  • Verify the path and selected Gateway; refresh the directory listing if the file moved.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended required resource exists and its current identity is verified.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
